examples.en: I toil in the garden the whole weekend.

examples.sr: Сваки дан [шља̏кам] од осам до пет.
examples.en: I work like a dog from eight to five every day.
He slogged away in the mine all his life.

examples.sr: Моја мајка [р̏мбачи] од јутра до мрака.
examples.en: My mother works her fingers to the bone from morning till night.

related.en: to slave away, to toil — hard, monotonous work, often for little pay
to grind, to work hard — the most common of the four
to work like a horse — until exhausted
to slog, to keep at it — stubbornly and for long hours

note: All four verbs are colloquial and almost interchangeable. The neutral verb is ра́дити.

examples.en: Let's meet at the kafana after work.
Beer is cheap at the dive.
We had dinner at a nice mehana.

examples.sr: Стара [кр̏чма] на путу ради и данас.
examples.en: The old inn on the road is still open today.

related.en: tavern-café — a place with food, beer, rakija and music
dive, cheap pub — a simple, inexpensive place
old-style inn — often deliberately stylized
inn, tavern — an old word, sounds bookish

note: The neutral word is кафа̀на. Бѝртија sounds jokingly dismissive, while меха̀на and кр̏чма evoke the old days.

examples.en: This bread is hard.
He has a strong character.

related.en: hard — about consistency: тврдо дрво, тврда подлога
firm, sturdy — чврст мост, чврст карактер

note: Тврда вода is hard water. The solid state of matter is чвр̑сто ста́ње.

examples.en: We bought a cake for the birthday.
We tie the tomatoes to a stake.

related.en: cake, pastry, cookie — sweet baked goods
stake, pole — a wooden stick driven into the ground

note: The words differ only in the last letter, and in Latin script without diacritics (kolac, kolac) they are identical.

examples.en: The baby is sucking milk.
The barber has been cutting my hair for years.

related.en: to suck — milk, a lollipop
to cut hair; шишати се - to get a haircut

note: Without diacritics in Latin script both verbs are spelled the same (sisati), so they are easy to mix up in chat. Cyrillic has no such problem.

examples.en: The money is in the bank.
We have a jar of pickles.

related.en: bank — a financial institution
glass jar — for jam, pickles, ajvar

note: A jar of jam is a те́гла. A tin can is лѝме̄нка.

examples.en: Do you have anything fasting-friendly?

examples.sr: Данас је [мр̏сан] ручак: пита са месом.
examples.en: Today's lunch is not for fasting: meat pie.

related.en: lenten, fasting food — without meat, dairy or eggs
non-fasting food — meat and dairy, when fasting is not observed

note: Посна храна is food allowed during a fast, мрсна храна is ordinary food with meat and dairy.

meanings: црни лук, бели лук or медвеђи лук?

examples.en: Chop an onion for the salad.
Garlic goes into the dish.

examples.sr: У пролеће берем [мѐдвеђӣ лу̏к] у шуми.
examples.en: In spring I pick wild garlic in the woods.

related.en: onion — the ordinary bulb onion
garlic
ramsons, wild garlic — a wild spring onion; also сремуш

note: The color is no guide: цр̑нӣ лу̏к (literally black onion) is just an ordinary onion, and бе̑лӣ лу̏к (white onion) is garlic.

meanings: претворити се, правити се or остваривати се?

examples.en: Love turned into hatred.
He pretends to be sorry.
My dream is coming true.

related.en: to turn into — to change into another state
to pretend, to act as if
to come true, to be realized — a dream, a plan

examples.en: There are big differences between them.
I didn't leave for that reason.

related.en: divergence, discord — from разилазити се
reason

note: One vowel changes the meaning.

examples.en: He got a good grade in math.
It is hard to give an assessment of the situation.

related.en: grade, mark, rating — a school grade, an evaluation of work
assessment, estimate — an assessment of a situation

note: The verbs: оце́нити ра̑д - to evaluate work, проценити ситуацију - to assess the situation.

examples.en: Fill in the sentences with the appropriate forms.
This place is suitable for a vacation.

related.en: corresponding, appropriate — fitting a form or requirement
suitable, convenient — for a purpose, place or moment

note: По̏годан usually goes with «за»: по̏годан за о̀дмор.

examples.en: That was the first attempt.
There was an assassination attempt on the president.

related.en: attempt — any kind
assassination, attack — on the life of a well-known person

note: An attempt on someone's life is an атѐнта̄т, not a по̏куша̄ј.

skip: Russian-only confusion between «уединение» and «объединение»; the two Serbian words are unrelated for an English speaker

examples.en: Tell me the truth.
We are seeking justice for everyone.

related.en: truth — what corresponds to the facts
justice, fairness — by law and morality

note: In everyday speech «the truth» is и̏стина, while пра̑вда is justice.

meanings: отворити рачун or дати први гол?

examples.en: Yesterday I opened an account at the bank.

examples.sr: Домаћини су [да̏ли пр̑ви го̑л] у петом минуту.
examples.en: The home team scored the opening goal in the fifth minute.

related.en: to open a bank account — only at a bank
to score the first goal — to open the scoring in a game

note: «To open the scoring» is not translated literally. The score of a game is резу̀лта̄т, a draw is не̏решено.

examples.en: He showers the children with toys.
He gave Mom flowers.

related.en: to give someone gifts, to shower with gifts
to give someone a gift

note: Same meaning, different government: дари́вати takes the accusative and the instrumental, покло̀нити the dative and the accusative.

examples.en: We buy food at the market.
Everyone has their own lot, their own bread to earn.

related.en: food — the neutral everyday word
fated sustenance, daily bread — a bookish word

note: Нафака is a Turkism from a religious context: the sustenance destined for a person. You will not hear it in a shop.

examples.en: I'm slicing carrots for the salad.
Carrots are good for your eyesight.

related.en: carrot — common in Serbia
carrot — a synonym, also a standard word

note: There is no difference in meaning: Serbian allows parallel standard words. The same goes for бу̀ндева and ти̏ква (pumpkin), су́сед and ко̀мшија (neighbor).

examples.en: I like boiled rice.
I bought a bag of rice.

related.en: rice — the main word
rice — the variant used in neighboring regions

note: They are synonyms: ри́жа is the variant of neighboring regions, such as Croatia.

examples.en: We're going to the vineyard for the grape harvest.
I bought sweet grapes.

related.en: vineyard — the place, not the fruit
grapes — the fruit, as food

note: Serbian вѝногра̄д is the place where grapes grow, while the fruit itself is гро̑жђе.

examples.en: The gardener is buying fertilizer.
Don't throw trash in the street.

related.en: fertilizer — for soil, in agriculture
garbage, trash — also a rude insult

note: Said of a person, ђу̏бре is a rude insult: «scum».

examples.en: I can't run, my leg hurts.
What are you running away from?
The police are chasing the thief through the city.

related.en: to run — on foot; sports, jogging
to flee, to run away — from someone or out of a country
to chase, to race — after someone or something; to pursue

note: Any running on foot is тр̀чати, while бѐжати always means to flee or run away.

examples.en: I got an answer.
Yesterday I received your message.
She made a lot of friends.
We got tickets for the concert.

related.en: to get, to receive — the most general word
to receive, to accept — a message, signal, letter, salary
to acquire, to gain — non-material things: experience, friends, recognition
to get hold of, to procure — things: tickets, weapons

note: До̀бити works almost everywhere, even for unpleasant things: добити корпу - to be turned down.

examples.en: What is the capacity of this pitcher?
The circumference of the head is fifty-eight centimeters.
This shampoo gives hair volume.

related.en: volume, capacity — liters, cubic meters
circumference, girth; scope — waist, head; scale of work
volume, fullness — of hair; loudness of sound

note: English «volume» is split here into three words: capacity, length of an outline, and fullness.

examples.en: Which movie are you watching?
What kind of movies do you like?
How much is your salary?

related.en: which — a choice from a known set: a title, number, day
what kind of — by quality: properties, genre, type
how big, how much — size, amount

note: Quantity and price are asked with колико: Колико кошта? - «How much does it cost?»

examples.sr: Умотај колач у [та̏бак] папира за печење.
examples.en: Wrap the cake in a sheet of baking paper.
It is written on paper.
He sold securities.
My grandfather grows tobacco.

related.en: sheet of paper — a single or printed sheet
paper — the material and the general word; documents
paper — formal: securities, a scrap of paper
tobacco for smoking — the plant and the raw material

note:
Don't be misled by the look: tobacco is ду̀ва̄н, while та̏бак is a sheet of paper.

Папири in the plural means «documents», тоалетни папир is toilet paper.

examples.en: I'm drinking hot chocolate.
Give me a glass of lukewarm water.
The tea is too hot.

related.en: warm, hot — water, food, drinks
lukewarm, tepid — room temperature
very hot — scalding tea, hot weather

note: То̏пао is wider than English «warm»: it is also used for hot dishes and drinks, for example то̏пла̄ чокола́да.

examples.en: I don't know a single word.
He neither drinks nor smokes.
I'll come too.

related.en: not even, no — strengthens a negation
nor, neither — joins negative parts: нити ... нити
and, also, too — in an affirmative statement

note: «Me too» is usually «и ја̑», not «ја такође».

examples.sr: Имам [о̏сећа̄ј] да нешто није у реду.
examples.en: I have a feeling that something is wrong.
She showed her feelings.
Emotions influence thinking.

related.en: sensation, hunch — of cold, of guilt
feeling — a lasting emotional experience, often in the plural
emotion — more often in psychology and science

note: О̏сећа̄ј is what you feel right now, or a vague hunch. О̀сећа̄ње is deeper. The line is loose and the words often overlap.

examples.en: Some mushrooms are poisonous.

examples.sr: Лекар је рекао да је то [гљѝвица].
examples.en: The doctor said it's a fungal infection.
We're going mushroom picking in the morning.

related.en: mushroom, fungus — the neutral, scientific word; edible and poisonous
small mushroom; fungal infection — a diminutive or a disease
mushroom — the everyday word: forest, kitchen, picking

note: Пѐчӯрка sounds more everyday, гљи̏ва more bookish, and гљивица most often means a fungal infection.

examples.en: The worker accepted our offer.

examples.sr: Она жели развод, али ја не [прѝстајем].
examples.en: She wants a divorce, but I don't agree.
I agree with you.

related.en: to accept, to agree to — an offer, rules, an idea
to agree to, to consent to — a condition, an action
to agree with — a person or an opinion

note: Government: прѝстати на + acc., сло̀жити се са + instr.

examples.en: Did you throw out the trash?
Quit smoking, it's harmful.
I'll be leaving the city soon.

related.en: to throw, to throw away — an object: trash, a coin
to leave, to quit — a habit or a person
to leave, to abandon — a place or a person

note: О̀ставити also means simply «to leave somewhere»: Оставио сам телефон код куће.

meanings: to meet: срести (се), састати се, видети се, наћи се, окупити се

examples.en: I ran into him in town by chance.
Tonight we're meeting with our colleagues.
See you tomorrow!
Where shall we meet?
The citizens gathered in the square.

related.en: to meet, to run into — by chance, an unexpected meeting
to meet — by arrangement, a business or planned meeting
to see each other — to keep in touch
to meet — at an agreed place
to gather — many people in one place

note: «See you!» in Serbian is видимо се.

meanings: to meet: упознати, дочекати, забављати се, наићи (на), јавити се

examples.sr: У Србији сам [упо̀знао] много занимљивих људи.
examples.en: In Serbia I met many interesting people.
Will you meet me at the airport?
Luka is dating the pharmacist.

examples.sr: [На̀ишао] сам на ову реч у уџбенику.
examples.en: I came across this word in a textbook.
This illness occurs in children.

related.en: to get to know, to meet for the first time — a new acquaintance
to meet, to welcome — an arriving person; to wait for, to live to see
to date, to go out — a relationship
to come across, to stumble upon — to find by chance
to occur, to appear — of phenomena

note:
There are other meanings:
• ја́вити се - «to get in touch»: Јави ми се кад стигнеш
• за̀бављати се - «to have fun»

meanings: to settle in: сместити се, уклопити се, снаћи се, запослити се

examples.en: Make yourselves more comfortable.

examples.sr: Како ћу се [укло̀пити] у нову средину?
examples.en: How will I fit into the new environment?
I found my feet in the new place.
I got a job at a shop.

related.en: to settle in, to get accommodated — in a place, in housing
to fit in — with a group, an environment, an interior
to find one's feet, to manage — to cope on your own
to get a job

note: English «to settle in» has no single Serbian verb: it depends on what is being settled - housing, a place in a group, affairs or a job.

meanings: to take: узети, понети, изабрати, брати

examples.en: Take what you want.
Take the documents with you.
Which dress did you choose?
We were picking mushrooms in the forest.

related.en: to take — by hand, to buy, to take medicine
to take along, to bring
to choose, to pick — from several
to pick, to gather — fruit, flowers, mushrooms

note: In a café you order like this: У̀зе̄ћу јо̀гурт - «I'll have a yogurt». Coffee to go: по̀нети.

examples.en: I am asking for a pardon.
He is asking for a raise.
I beg you not to interrupt me.
The man asked what had happened.

related.en: to ask for, to demand; to look for
to ask, to beg — politely: please, to ask Dad for something
to ask — a question

note: Trap: пи́тати means only «to ask a question», never «to ask for something». For a request use мо̀лити or тра́жити.

meanings: сећати се, осећати or осећати се?

examples.en: I don't remember what his name is.
Do plants feel pain?
How are you feeling today?

related.en: to remember, to recall — + gen.
to feel something — pain, a smell
to feel (a certain way) — how you feel

note: The words differ by one letter and only sound alike. Се̏ћати се takes the genitive: сећам се његовог имена.

examples.sr: Не [мо̑ра̄ш] да радиш ако не желиш.
examples.en: You don't have to work if you don't want to.
You are not allowed to smoke here.
You have to work, you have no choice.

related.en: must, to have to — necessity
may, to be allowed to — permission

note: In the negative the meaning differs: не мо̑ра̄ш - «you don't have to», не сме̑ш - «you must not».

examples.en: I'll call you later.
The phone is ringing, answer it.
Ring the doorbell.

related.en: to call, to phone someone — + acc.
to ring — of a sound

note: Зва̏ти takes the accusative: зовем брата. Зво̀нити is about a sound: a phone, a doorbell, a bell.

examples.en: I think it's important.
I was counting money.
I was counting on your help.

related.en: to consider, to think — an opinion
to count — numbers, objects
to calculate, to count on — arithmetic, a calculation

note: Рачу̀нати на + acc. - «to count on, to rely on»: рачунам на тебе.

meanings: to communicate: дружити се, причати, комуницирати

examples.en: We've been hanging out lately.
Go, have a chat with your uncle.

examples.sr: Важно је да редовно [комунѝцираш] са клијентима.
examples.en: It is important to communicate with clients regularly.

related.en: to hang out, to socialize — friendly relations
to talk, to have a chat — to discuss something
to communicate, to be in touch — business or informational contact

note: Trap: better not to use општити for «to communicate»: to Serbs it can sound like an awkward hint of sexual intimacy.

meanings: to need, to demand: требати, захтевати, тражити

examples.en: I need new shoes.
The workers are demanding higher wages.
Friendship takes effort.

related.en: to be needed, to need — does not mean «to demand»
to demand, to insist; to imply — firmly
to ask for, to demand, to look for — softer than захтевати

note: Trap: тре̏бати does not mean «to require». Захте́вати is a firm demand, тра́жити is a request or a search.

meanings: to cook, to make: кувати, спремати, правити

examples.en: Mom cooks wonderfully.
Today we're having a barbecue.
I prepared a light dinner.

related.en: to cook, to boil — soup, potatoes, coffee, goulash
to prepare, to get ready — food, a wedding, a talk
to make — a dish, by its name

note: Pancakes, salad and grilled food are not «boiled»: say правити палачинке, направити салату.

examples.en: Look out the window.
We have free appointment slots tomorrow at 12.
I have a gap in my schedule from three to six.

examples.sr: Службеница на [ша̀лтеру] број 3 је задужена за то.
examples.en: The clerk at counter number 3 is in charge of that.

related.en: window — an opening in a wall
appointment slot — a booked time with a doctor, a stylist
gap, break — free time between classes
counter, service window — at a bank, a post office, an office

note: You book an appointment like this: зака́зати тѐрмӣн.

meanings: to live, to stay: живети, становати, одсести

examples.en: Where do you live?
Have you been living here long?
In Belgrade we stayed at a hotel.

related.en: to live — in general, permanently
to reside — with a place given
to stay, to put up — temporarily: at a hotel, with acquaintances

note: You stay at a hotel with одсѐсти, while жи́вети implies a permanent home.

meanings: to carry, to bear, to postpone, to move: носити/преносити, подносити, одлагати, померати

examples.en: Mosquitoes carry diseases.
I can't stand the heat.
We have already postponed the meeting twice.

examples.sr: Можемо ли да [помѐримо] час за пола сата?
examples.en: Can we move the class by half an hour?

related.en: to carry, to transfer; to transmit — things, diseases
to bear, to stand — heat, stress, pain
to postpone, to put off — a meeting, a flight
to move, to shift — a time or a place

note: Но̀сити also means «to wear (clothes)»: Носи наочаре.

meanings: to do, to study: бавити се, учити, проучавати, радити

examples.en: What sport do you do?
I'm studying in the library.
Scientists are studying climate change.
What do you do after work?

related.en: to be engaged in, to do — a hobby, work, science
to learn, to study — lessons, a language
to study, to research — in depth, in science
to do, to work — what you are occupied with

note: Ба̏вити се is not used without a complement: say what with (instr.): бавим се спортом.

key: cmp:примати-туширати се, купати се, сунчати се-узимати
meanings: to take: примати, узимати, туширати се

examples.en: We don't receive visitors.

examples.sr: Лекар је препоручио да [узѝмам] таблете два пута дневно.
examples.en: The doctor recommended that I take the pills twice a day.
I take a shower several times a day.

related.en: to receive, to accept — gifts, guests, visitors
to take — medicine; to take into account

related.sr: туши́рати се, ку́пати се, су̀нчати се
related.en: to take a shower, a bath, a sunbath — reflexive verbs

note: «To take part» is у̀чествовати, not при́мати.

key: cmp:донети одлуку-положити заклетву-предузети мере-прихватити понуду-усвојити закон
meanings: to pass, to make, to take, to accept in set phrases

examples.en: Parliament passed a new law.
We made the decision on our own.
I am taking every precaution.
I accept your offer.
The new judge took the oath.

related.en: to pass a law — parliament, a document
to make a decision
to take measures
to accept an offer — to agree
to take an oath — on taking office

note: In these phrases the verb is not при́мати: learn each phrase as a whole.

meanings: to undress: свући се, скинути се, раскомотити се

examples.sr: Сад се [сву̀ци] и легни на леђа.
examples.en: Now undress and lie on your back.
Just take off your hat.
Come in, make yourself comfortable.

related.en: to take off, to undress — literally «to pull off»
to take off, to undress
to take off extra clothes and settle in — what you offer to guests

note: Do not say скини се to a guest: it sounds like «get undressed». To invite them to take off their coat and settle in, say раскомоти се.

examples.en: Open the door.

examples.sr: [О̀ткрио] сам да мој пријатељ има канал.
examples.en: I found out that my friend has a channel.
I can't unlock my phone.

related.en: to open something closed; to begin — a door, a window, a session
to discover, to reveal — to uncover the unknown
to unlock — with a key; a lock, a screen

note: О̀ткрити also means «to unveil» a monument: о̀ткрити спо̏менӣк.

examples.en: I don't know how to play chess.
When did you learn to play the guitar?
Who acted in that movie?

related.en: to play — a game, a sport; to dance
to play an instrument; to sound — of music
to act, to play a role — in theater, film; to pretend

note: Ѝграти ко̏ло - «to dance the kolo».

examples.en: I closed the window.

examples.sr: Не сећам се да сам [закљу̀чао] врата.
examples.en: I don't remember locking the door.
Put the lid on the pot.

related.en: to close — a window, a book, a door without locking
to lock — with a key
to cover, to put a lid on — a pot, eyes with a palm

note: The opposites: отво̀рити - «to open», откљу̏чати - «to unlock».

examples.en: The boy broke his arm.
Who broke the toy?
The elevator broke down yesterday.

related.en: to break, to crush — a bone, a will, a heart
to break, to spoil — a toy, a device

note: The noun is ква̑р: Лифт је у квару - «the elevator is out of order».

meanings: to clean up, to remove: склонити, уклонити, спремити, очистити

examples.en: Move the camera away.
We removed the spam from the site.
I tidied up the room.
How can I remove limescale?

related.en: to put away, to move aside — out of sight, to the side
to remove, to get rid of — for good: spam, an obstacle
to tidy up, to put in order; to prepare — a room, an apartment
to clean, to clear off dirt — limescale, a yard, vegetables

note: Спре́мити also means «to prepare, to pack»: спре́мити ру́чак, спремити ствари.

examples.en: Some mushrooms are poisonous.
There are a lot of mushrooms in the forest.
I bought a cream for fungal infections.

related.en: mushrooms, fungi — the broadest word, any kind
mushrooms — with cap and stem, edible and poisonous
fungus, mold — infections and mildew

note: At a pharmacy ask for a cream against гљивица: «крем за печурке» would not be understood.

examples.sr: Хтео сам нешто да ти кажем, [за̀то̄] сам те звао.
examples.en: I wanted to tell you something, that's why I called.

examples.sr: Кућа је без намештаја, али [за̀то̄] пуна књига.
examples.en: The house has no furniture, but it is full of books instead.
The elevator is out of order, so we are taking the stairs.

related.en: therefore, that's why; but on the other hand — neutral, much more common in speech
therefore, hence — bookish, formal

note: Only за̀то̄ has the second meaning: «but in return».

meanings: very: јако, веома, врло, баш, много, пуно

examples.en: I'm very sorry.
That is very important.
He is very kind.

examples.sr: Нашла сам [ба̏ш] оно што сам тражила.
examples.en: I found exactly what I was looking for.
I like this city a lot.
I love you a lot.

related.en: very, strongly — colloquial
very, quite — the most neutral
very — more often in writing, with adjectives and adverbs
exactly, just; quite — emphasis
a lot; very — quantity, degree, strength of action
a lot — quantity; not with adjectives

note:
For «very» with an adjective use вѐома, вр̏ло, ја̑ко, мно̏го, but not пу̏но: you don't say пу̏но до̏бар.

Ба̏ш before a noun means «exactly this»: ба̏ш о̀во̄.
